record.original_question: For a connected simple algebraic group G, let Cay(G) denote the minimum degree of a dominant rational G-equivariant map from G, with G acting by conjugation, to its Lie algebra Lie G, with G acting via the adjoint representation. What are the Cayley degrees Cay(G) of the connected simple algebraic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $G$ be a connected simple algebraic group over $k$ with Lie algebra $\mathrm{Lie}(G)$. Consider $G$ as a $G$-variety via the conjugation action, and consider $\mathrm{Lie}(G)$ as a $G$-variety via the adjoint representation. A dominant rational map $\varphi\colon G \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(G)$ is called $G$-equivariant if $\varphi(g x g^{-1}) = \mathrm{Ad}(g)\,\varphi(x)$ as rational maps. The degree of such a $\varphi$ is the degree of the induced extension of function fields $[k(G):\varphi^*k(\mathrm{Lie}(G))]$. Define the Cayley degree
$$\mathrm{Cay}(G) \;=\; \min\{\deg(\varphi) : \varphi\colon G \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Lie}(G)\text{ dominant rational }G\text{-equivariant}\}.$$
Determine $\mathrm{Cay}(G)$ for every connected simple algebraic group $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: Lemire, Popov, and Reichstein (2006) classified which simple algebraic groups are Cayley (i.e., have Cay(G)=1), and the stably Cayley case has been settled in characteristic zero (Borovoi–Kunyavskii–Lemire–Reichstein, 2014). However, no general formula for the Cayley degree Cay(G) of arbitrary connected simple algebraic groups appears in the literature; the problem of computing Cay(G) in all cases remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: Lemire, Popov, Reichstein classify Cayley simple groups; Cay(G)=1 only for specific groups.
status_evidence.claim: The Cay(G)=1 case is classified, but general Cay(G) values are not determined.

status_evidence.snippet: Classifies stably Cayley simple groups in characteristic zero.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses stably Cayley classification but not the general Cayley degree.
